title: Tu familia o la mía
desc: Whose house you go to, and what it stands for
setting: It is the twenty-third of December and both mothers are expecting you.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Mi mamá ya contó con nosotros para el veinticuatro.
steps.en: My mother has already counted on us for the twenty-fourth.

options.es: Va. ¿Y qué hacemos con doña Carmen entonces?
options.en: Right. And what do we do about doña Carmen then?
options.feedback: Accepted her mother, then asked about yours in the same breath. Nobody has been chosen over anybody.

options.en: And you already told her yes?
options.feedback: The question underneath is fair. Asked like that, it is about permission rather than the plan.

options.en: It is always your mother first.
options.feedback: Siempre turns one December into every December. Now you are arguing about the last four years.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Podemos pasar por donde ella temprano.
steps.en: We can go by hers early.

options.es: Eso me parece bien. Yo le aviso hoy mismo.
options.en: That sounds good to me. I will tell her today.
options.feedback: Accepted and you took the job of telling her. That half is yours and doing it fast is what keeps it small.

options.en: All right, if there is time.
options.feedback: A yes with a way out already in it. She will hear the way out.

options.es: Temprano no le sirve a ella.
options.en: Early is no good for her.
options.feedback: Perhaps not. Now there is no plan at all and it is your turn to make one.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿Vos creés que se va a poner brava?
steps.en: Do you think she will get upset?

options.es: Un poco, pero se le pasa. Prefiero decírselo yo.
options.en: A little, but she will get over it. I would rather tell her myself.
options.feedback: Honest about the cost and you take it on yourself. That is the whole answer.
Comfortable, and probably wrong. She asked because she thinks so.
Said about your own mother to your wife, it will be remembered by both of them.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Gracias. Yo sé que no es fácil.
steps.en: Thank you. I know it is not easy.

options.es: Ninguno de los dos tiene familia de sobra.
options.en: Neither of us has family to spare.
options.feedback: It puts the two of you on the same side of a thing that has no clean answer. Nothing else needed saying.
It waves away something she just acknowledged. She was being kind.
That is the argument you avoided all afternoon, arriving at the end anyway.
